title: Using the map instead of walking the shop
target: How the maps work in Supermarket Simulator: the minimap and the larger map as separate pieces, the cursor the larger map tracks, the markers that belong to fixtures, the tooltip, the online-order customer's own target, and pinging a spot for the other players.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that is open with something worth finding
The map opened at least once so you know where it sits
Another player if you intend to ping something

steps.do: Treat the small map and the large one as two different things.
steps.because: the game keeps a minimap and a larger map as separate pieces, so the corner of the screen and the map you open are not the same view at two sizes (MiniMap, MiniMapTracker)

steps.do: Use the cursor on the larger map rather than chasing your own position.
steps.because: the larger map tracks a cursor of its own, so you can look at part of the shop without walking there (GlobalMapCursor)

steps.do: Read the markers rather than searching the aisles.
steps.because: markers are objects of their own, including ones for particular fixtures, so what you own can be shown on the map instead of only found by eye (GlobalMapMarker, VendingGlobalMapUIMarker)

steps.do: Hover a marker before you act on it.
steps.because: the map has a tooltip of its own, so a marker can be identified without leaving the map (MapTooltip)

steps.do: In a shared shop, expect one map for everyone.
steps.because: the minimap is tracked on the network, so a marker one player sees is a marker the crew shares (NetworkMinimapTracker)

steps.do: When an online order arrives, look for its own target before hunting for the customer.
steps.because: a customer arriving through an online order has a map target of its own rather than using an ordinary one (OnlineOrderCustomerMinimapCustomTarget)

steps.do: Ping a spot rather than describing it aloud.
steps.because: there is a ping marker for pointing something out to another player, so a shelf or a spill can be marked instead of explained (PingMarker)

steps.do: Do not plan the whole shop from the map alone.
steps.because: the map shows what has markers rather than everything on the floor, so the layout still has to be walked to be judged (GlobalMapMarker, MiniMap)

commonMistakes: Treating the minimap as the map and never opening the larger one.
Searching the shop by eye for things that carry a marker.
Hunting for an online-order customer without using its map target.
Describing a location to another player instead of pinging it.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
